bull_bear.body:
- Innovator, patent-protected specialist portfolio backed by the global AstraZeneca group's asset pipeline across oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology
- Regulatory throughput: 20 product approvals (including label expansions) secured since FY24-25, with 13 approvals in FY25-26 alone
- Oncology leadership - described as the Company's most powerful growth engine in India, propelling it into the top 2 oncology players by revenue
- Brand durability after loss of exclusivity: Brilinta remains market leader growing at double digit despite LOE in 2019 and entry of close to 40 generics; Lynparza retains market leadership by value share with over 16 biosimilar entrants; Forxiga is among the top 5 brands of Dapagliflozin by value despite 600+ dapagliflozin brands
- First-to-market specialist launches - Soliris, India's first anti-complement therapy, and Lokelma, one of the best launches of 2025 by 1st month sales value
- Fastest-growing among top companies by revenue in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market in FY 2025-26, growing faster than the top 25 companies and gaining 2 spots to rank #37
- Robust clinical operations and evidence-generation capability used to accelerate regulatory milestones in India
- Asset-light India model - distribution and marketing led, with manufacturing decommissioned and product supply sourced under long-standing group formulation, packaging and distribution agreements
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Loss of the India manufacturing footprint following factory closure — The BRSR records a single national site at which manufacturing activities were ceased during the year under review, leaving the entity dependent on group supply for its products and removing in-country production flexibility.
- Workforce disruption and elevated attrition from the factory closure — All permanent workers left during the year on account of redundancies from the factory closure, and permanent-employee turnover remains a disclosed watch-item across the last three years - a retention and knowledge-continuity risk for a specialist-selling organisation.
- Concentration on a single business activity and a narrow customer set — The entity's main activity is marketing and trading of pharmaceutical products, sold pan-India to a customer base of distributors, hospitals and Government institutions, with international sales limited to one country (Nepal) - leaving little diversification if that channel or activity is disrupted.
- Dependence on a single holding company within the AstraZeneca group — AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals AB is disclosed as the Holding Company and the reporting boundary is standalone; product supply, pricing and portfolio choices therefore sit largely with the group rather than with the listed entity.
- Product quality and customer complaint exposure — Complaints received under the responsible-business-conduct principles from customers mainly pertain to Product Quality Complaints in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, a recurring quality/pharmacovigilance watch-item for a marketing-and-distribution entity.
- Climate transition and value-chain (Scope 3) emissions exposure — Scope 3 emissions represent approximately 98% of the total footprint and come primarily from purchased goods and services, capital goods, distribution and product use - so decarbonisation depends on suppliers and logistics the Company does not directly control.
- Nature, water and pollution dependencies across the value chain — Natural resources are described as fundamental to the discovery, development and manufacture of medicines; the Company manages sustainable sourcing, water and circular resource use, pollution minimisation and pharmaceuticals in the environment (PIE) against 2030 site targets.
- Governance and leadership transition churn — The Managing Director and two Non-Executive Directors ceased office during FY 2025-26, with consequential turnover in the chairs and membership of the Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship and Risk Management Committees.
- Enterprise risk categories formally identified by the Board — The Risk Management Committee's mandate covers financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (particularly ESG-related), information and cyber security risks, with a business continuity plan and a policy reviewed at least once in two years; the Committee met twice during the financial year.

business.body: The Company is engaged in the business of distribution and marketing of pharmaceutical products in India and co-ordinates clinical trial services with an overseas group company; its manufacturing operations were decommissioned during the year under review. Sales and marketing operations are internally structured around three business verticals - Biopharmaceuticals Business Unit, Oncology Business Unit and Rare Disease Unit - with the portfolio focused on Oncology, Cardiovascular, Renal, Metabolism and Respiratory, alongside recent expansion into Rare Diseases. All of the Company's activities fall within a single business segment, so separate segment-wise disclosures are not provided.

outlook.body:
- Focus the India portfolio on Oncology, Cardiovascular, Renal, Metabolism and Respiratory, alongside recent expansion into Rare Diseases
- Operate sales and marketing through three business verticals - Biopharmaceuticals Business Unit, Oncology Business Unit and Rare Disease Unit (the latter launched in 2023)
- Grow through innovation: introduce new innovative products and secure label / indication expansions to deepen and broaden the existing therapy-area portfolio
- Tap the group's asset pipeline to bring life-changing medicines in oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology to Indian patients at the earliest, subject to feasibility and regulatory approvals
- Leverage robust clinical operations and evidence-generation capabilities to accelerate regulatory milestones in India
- Continue to prioritise investments in the Company's focus disease areas, in line with its strategy
- Run an asset-light India model - the Company is engaged in distribution and marketing of pharmaceutical products and co-ordinates clinical trial services with an overseas group company, its manufacturing operations having been decommissioned during the year under review
- The Company maintains a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on its website; the annual-report text provided sets out the policy's existence rather than a numeric payout philosophy. Governance of remuneration and appointments runs through a formal Nomination and Remuneration Policy covering Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Executives, supported by a vigil mechanism / whistle-blowing policy with direct access to the Audit Committee Chairperson in exceptional cases. On the deployment side the model is deliberately asset-light: no capital investment was made in energy conservation equipment because the factory is undergoing the closure process, and the Company confirms there are no materially significant related party transactions with Promoters, Directors, KMP or Senior Management that may have a potential conflict of interest, with all related-party dealings during FY 2025-26 in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis.
- Ambition Zero Carbon - a $1bn global programme investing in reducing GHG emissions across the research, development, manufacture and supply of medicines
- 88% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions (from sites and fleet) achieved since 2015 while more than doubling revenue, with continued progress targeted
- Tackling Scope 3 (value chain) emissions, which represent approximately 98% of the total footprint, through product innovation including transition to the next-generation propellant, supplier engagement, sustainable transport (shifting from air to sea freight) and responsible business travel
- 2030 targets focused on water stewardship and circularity across sites, complemented by governance and metrics to track performance and scale investments
- Nature action: sustainable sourcing and circular resource use to prevent land use change, deforestation and exploitation of natural resources
- Pollution minimisation: tracking of the waste circularity rate and recognised industry leadership in managing pharmaceuticals in the environment (PIE)
- Nature restoration through global programmes including AZ Forest, working with stakeholders such as indigenous peoples and local communities
- Sustainability strategy built on action on climate and nature, health equity and health systems resilience, delivered in collaboration with governments, health systems, patient groups, academia and NGOs
- Board-level oversight of sustainability risk: ESG-related risks are explicitly within the Risk Management Committee's risk-identification framework
- BRSR reported on a standalone basis with Limited Assurance on BRSR Core Indicators by KPMG Assurance and Consulting Services LLP
- Women represent 83.33% of the Board of Directors and 66.7% of Key Management Personnel
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, anchored on the published Code of Ethics
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company has no manufacturing capex or capacity-addition programme in this report - its manufacturing operations were decommissioned during the year under review, leaving an India model built on distribution and marketing of pharmaceutical products plus co-ordination of clinical trial services with an overseas group company. Expansion is therefore portfolio-led rather than plant-led: sales and marketing are organised around three verticals (Biopharmaceuticals Business Unit, Oncology Business Unit and the Rare Disease Unit launched in 2023), and growth comes from new molecule introductions and label / indication expansions. The Company secured 20 product approvals including label expansions since FY24-25, with 13 within FY25-26 alone, adding Datverzo in Oncology (unresectable or metastatic breast cancer with relevant mutations) and securing indication extensions across lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction and other tumour types; separately the Board's report notes 11 regulatory approvals for medicines and indications during the year. Capability building beyond the medicine continued through AI-led lung cancer detection, diagnostic capability building, clinical education, Rare Disease advocacy and wider health system partnerships. The remaining site-level capital decision is closure-related: no capital investment was made in energy conservation equipment because the factory is undergoing the closure process.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian Pharmaceutical Market is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 8.7% between 2025 and 2028, touching approximately USD 33 billion by 2027
- Indian healthcare industry projected to grow at 12% CAGR through 2028, driven by both private and public healthcare expenditure and investments
- IPM value growth of 10% in FY 2025-26, an acceleration from ~9% in the previous fiscal, with price adjustments contributing 44% of growth and volume expansion and new product introductions 27% and 28% respectively
- Ageing population and high non-communicable disease burden - over 100 million people in India afflicted with diabetes, rising to 139 million by 2035; cardiovascular disease the leading cause of death and COPD the second; cancer incidence expected to rise above 2 million new cases by 2040
- Expanding health insurance coverage - private health insurance expected to grow, PMJAY beneficiaries close to 440 million individuals, and the PMJAY expansion to all senior citizens aged 70 and above spanning an estimated 45 million households
- Rising incomes and affordability - high-income households expected to more than double in a decade, with an estimated 23 million households earning over Rs 2 million per annum
- Tax concessions improving patient access - broadening of the GST reduction from 12% to 5% on drugs and customs duty waivers for 17 oncology and 7 rare disease medications in the FY26-27 budget
- Growth of e-pharmacies, projected at upwards of USD 4 billion, expanding access and share of total pharmacy sales
- Strategic industry shift toward novel therapies, biologics and gene therapies, supported by policy initiatives such as Biopharma SHAKTI
- AI and digital adoption driving productivity across the value chain and telemedicine unlocking specialist access in remote regions
- Company-specific mix: the Oncology therapeutic area continued to outpace general market growth in FY 2025-26, while Respiratory and CVRM saw growth rates slightly lower than the overall market average
- Headwinds flagged: intensified pricing pressure from expanded drug price controls, intellectual property infringement risk, and supply chain vulnerabilities from persistent geopolitical uncertainties
- Robust asset pipeline available to the Company within therapy areas of oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology, subject to feasibility and regulatory approvals
- Recent launch and approval flow: 20 product approvals including label expansions since FY24-25, with 13 in FY25-26 - Datverzo in Oncology, Lokelma in Biopharmaceuticals, and Soliris in Rare Disease
- Oncology indication extensions secured in FY25-26 across lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, liver, bladder and endometrial cancer

deepdive.thesis: AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited is the Indian arm of a global, science-led, patient-focused biopharmaceutical group, marketing innovator specialist medicines across Oncology, Biopharmaceuticals and Rare Disease.

open.item: The Board has proposed, for Members' approval at the 47th Annual General Meeting, a dividend of Rs. 36 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26.
Having ceased operations at its Bangalore manufacturing site, the Company expects to sell the related assets within 12 months, and has classified them as held for sale.

The Company intends to expand its India portfolio further by tapping the group's asset pipeline in oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology, subject to feasibility and regulatory approvals.
The Company will continue to prioritise investments in its focus disease areas, in line with its strategy, and leverage its portfolio plus new product launches to sustain its IPM ranking momentum.

Management flags intensifying downward pressure on drug prices from potential NLEM expansion, more molecules under Schedule I of the DPCO, caps on trade mark-ups for non-scheduled products, and loss of exclusivity driving generic proliferation.

The Company commits to bring life-changing medicines across oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, respiratory and immunology and make them available to patients in India at the earliest, subject to feasibility and regulatory approvals.
The Company will continue to leverage its robust clinical operations and evidence-generation capabilities to further accelerate regulatory milestones in India.

Management flags that drug pricing pressure may intensify from potential NLEM expansion, more molecules under Schedule I of the DPCO, caps on trade mark-ups and loss of exclusivity driving generic proliferation.
Management flags geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain volatility, including Middle East tensions, energy cost escalation and currency depreciation, as threats to supply chain costs and volumes.
Management flags persistent patent infringement threats and circulation of counterfeit, spurious or illegally imported drugs as risks to value and patient safety.

Expansion is portfolio-led: the Company continues to introduce innovative products and secure label expansions across Oncology, Biopharmaceuticals and Rare Disease rather than add manufacturing capacity.
